parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Hi are you ready to discuss our presentation?

Yeah sure. So what are we going to say about teachers readingpicture books with young children?

Hmm. I think we should start with the reason why teachers use picture books.

The journal article we read mentioned several picture books and whythey're popular with teachers.

Right. Like, I spy friends, it's a lovely story.

Yeah. But children like to find the familiar faces from the fairy tales they know so well.

And they're all doing predictable things. The article said children finad this familiarity very comforting

Yes. Now, how about good night little rabbit, which has those delightf pictures? I love the way the colors get darker as the book progresses, indicating how evening turns into night.

Me too. The article said that's why teachers like it.

Very cute. And a good example of visual subtext, hard to believre that it came out over 60 years ago. It's still relevant.

I really liked what the article said about the boat party. There's alof repetition, which I think would be great for vocabulary development.

That's true. But apparently it's the images that make it popular withchildren The artist is really well known and children often ask for her books.

Oh, that's good to know.

And shall we also include puppy and friends?

Yes. It sounds like an innocent title. But the article warns that tthere's a bit of a fright, you know, the one on the last page when the puppy suddenly encounters the scary cat. Teacheers like to use this to help children explore their emotions.

Sounds good. Hats and socks is a good one. It doesn't really have a beginning and an end, does it? Which is unusual.

That's why teachers like this one, though. Because it's so different, it'sgood for children to hear a story that doesn't follow the usual pattern.

And the pages are so full of life and colour. A good choice.

Mmm.

Okay. And for our last one, how about a family adventure? This one uises a lot of the same language throughout, which

I think can help with letter and word recognition. Teachers say it hasa really poetic feel to it. They often sing it to a simple tune.

Yes. And it's full of beautiful watercolors too.

In the next part of our presentation, shall we look at some of the other research? I really liked Smith's article about the history of picture books. Picture books haven't been around for that long,of course. And as we know from our reading lists, there's a lot of research on them already. Smith makes some interesting points.

Yes, one thing that shocked me was that some people don't consider picture books as proper writing because they don't have enough words in them.

Yes, that was unexpected for me as well I think they should be just asrespected as other works of fiction. Smith also mentioned that books from other countries are very popular here, even thoughthey don't show our daily life. I think that's interesting.

But it's the same for adult fiction too. People want variety. What I didn't realize is how fixed the number of pages is.

Me neither. I wasn't expecting that they're so strictly limited to 32 p.ages. It's important, so let's include it.

All right. Now, let's think about other aspects of picture books vwe want to include in our presentation How about the characterrs?

Okay, well, a lot of them feature animals or families often in very traditional roles But do you think we need to talk about that?For me, the main thing is that they are mostly printed as board books. The cardboard material makes it easy for young children to turn their pages.

I agree. And it's essential for children to hold books and learn hhow they open at the front and that the text goes in a certain direection.

Good point. Why don't we also discuss how culture is importanin picture books, like the importance of respecting the elderly?

Yes, it's probably different all over the world. Would it be interestingto make a comparison between modern and historical picture books and consider future directions for the genre?

It sounds interesting, but I don't have any research on that, so vwe'd better leave it.

So what's next? We don't need it.

analyses.content: 男生提到孩子们喜欢在书中找到那些他们非常熟悉的童话故事里的“熟悉面孔（familiar faces）”，对应选项中的“著名角色（well-known characters）”。
Yeah. But children like to find the familiar faces from the fairy tales they know so well.
你可能听到“lovely story”想选其他褒义选项，但重点是 faces from fairy tales 对应的角色认知。
I love the way the colors get darker as the book progresses, indicating how evening turns into night.
你可能听到 visual subtext（视觉潜台词）觉得很深奥，但选项描述的是具体的画面内容变化。
女生说随着书的进行颜色变深，展示了“傍晚如何变成夜晚（evening turns into night）”，对应选项中的“时间变化（changing times of day）”。
But apparently it's the images that make it popular with children The artist is really well known and children often ask for her books.
男生先提到了 repetition（重复）对词汇好，但这只是他个人的看法，女生随后用 fact（显然是因为图画）进行了更正。
女生指出这本书之所以受孩子欢迎，是因为“插画师非常出名（The artist is really well known）”。
But the article warns that there's a bit of a fright, you know, the one on the last page when the puppy suddenly encounters the scary cat.
你可能听到 explore their emotions，但这只是老师使用这本书的目的，不是书本情节本身的特点。
录音提到虽然标题听起来无辜，但文章警告说最后一页有“惊吓（fright）”，小狗突然遇到了可怕的猫，这就是结尾的“惊喜/惊吓（surprise）”。
Hats and socks is a good one. It doesn't really have a beginning and an end, does it? Which is unusual. That's why teachers like this one...
女生后面提到了 life and colour，那是对书本视觉效果的评价，不是男生提出的核心特点。
男生说这本书没有真正的开头和结尾，这很不寻常（unusual），对应选项中的“不常见的情节结构（uncommon plot structure）”。
男生提到老师们说这本书很有诗意，经常把它唱成“简单的曲调（simple tune）”，对应选项中的“变成歌（turned into song）”。
Teachers say it has a really poetic feel to it. They often sing it to a simple tune.
虽然开头提到了 language 和 word recognition，但那是功能，最显著的特征是可以被唱出来。

questions.question: Which TWO points from Smith's article about picture books did both speakers find surprising?

analyses.content: Yes, one thing that shocked me was that some people don't consider picture books as proper writing because they don't have enough words in them.
你可能听到 research 或 history，但那些只是背景铺垫，真正引起震惊情绪的是关于“是不是文学”的争论。
女生说让她“震惊（shocked）”的是，有些人因为绘本字数少就不把它们当作“正经文学作品（proper writing）”。

analyses.content: What I didn't realize is how fixed the number of pages is. Me neither. I wasn't expecting that they're so strictly limited to 32 pages.
虽然提到了 books from other countries（海外书籍）很受欢迎，但女生说这很有趣，并没有说对此感到“惊讶（surprising）”，且男生认为成人小说也一样。
男生说他没意识到页数是多么“固定（fixed）”，女生也附和说没想到严格限制在 32 页，对应选项中的“标准长度”。

analyses.content: For me, the main thing is that they are mostly printed as board books. The cardboard material makes it easy for young children to turn their pages.
虽然前面提到了 animals, families 和 roles，但男生紧接着问“我们需要谈那个吗？”并在这个话题上转移了重点到材料上。
男生提议讨论它们大多印成“硬纸板书（board books/cardboard material）”，女生表示同意，这对应选项中的“制作材料”。

analyses.content: Why don't we also discuss how culture is important in picture books, like the importance of respecting the elderly?
结尾提到了 compare future directions（比较未来的方向），但女生直接说没有相关研究，所以“最好别谈（better leave it）”，直接排除了选项 E。
男生建议讨论“文化（culture）”在绘本中的重要性，比如尊重长辈，女生表示赞同。
